body:
Quiet day, no arbitrage found. A fresh scan of both venues turned up zero capturable opportunities — the standard state of affairs, since real arbitrage in these markets is rare and usually vanishes within seconds when it appears.

The prices on the board are consistent with what's actually happening in the metal. Gold has been grinding just under the $4,400 mark, and news from this week confirms it: spot XAU/USD was trading above $4,400 in European hours on August 17, reaching an intraday high of $4,416.43, while other trackers had it near $4,400 an ounce after ending the previous week almost 1% higher. That backdrop lines up neatly with Kalshi's gold above $4,371.99 settlement contract sitting near even money (55¢ bid / 63¢ ask) and Polymarket's touch $4,450 this week contract trading around 77–82¢ — both are pricing a metal that's already brushing against those levels, not a surprise. The rally itself has a clear driver: gold gained almost 1% the previous week, helped by data showing US consumer sentiment declined and retail sales posted their steepest monthly contraction in more than a year, which reduced the odds of a Fed rate hike and made non-yielding bullion more attractive.

Nothing in the book looks like free money — the near-100¢ prices on some far-out-of-the-money strikes reflect thin 24-hour volume rather than mispricing, and Kalshi's settle-price contracts aren't directly comparable to Polymarket's touch (intraday high/low) contracts, since the latter pays out on any wick through a level even if price closes elsewhere. That structural difference in resolution rules, not a market inefficiency, explains most of the apparent gaps between the two platforms today.
headline: No arbitrage found as gold prices near $4,400 align across platforms
